title: Germany tests IdentiFlight cameras for bird protection
summary: OekoFor and ARSU validated IdentiFlight at German test sites. Dated reports document red-kite and white-tailed eagle testing, without a measured reduction in German bird fatalities.
account: The OECD AI Incidents entry summarizes press coverage of 20 and 21 September 2022 (The Guardian, Mother Jones, The Register and others, not among the sources). It says that Germany is deploying AI-powered camera systems developed by IdentiFlight to detect endangered lesser spotted eagles near wind turbines and slow the blades to prevent collisions. The monitor's rationale cites the 82% reduction reported from the Wyoming study rather than a German measurement. OekoFor and ARSU compare camera detections with observations by ornithologists at German test sites. OekoFor’s dated updates report completion of red-kite validation in October 2021 and publication of a white-tailed eagle assessment in May 2023. These updates do not establish a German fatality-reduction estimate or the start date of the lesser spotted eagle tests.
purpose: IdentiFlight is built to detect eagles and curtail turbines; protecting lesser spotted eagles at German wind farms is the intended use.
system: IdentiFlight automated eagle detection and turbine curtailment
